review.summary:
approve_with_nits
The handoff explanation needs splitting for phone reading.
Two glossary entries define the same LangGraph term.
Validation: 25 tests passed; link checker reported bad 0. External sources were not verified offline.

findings.checklist_item: Plain language: paragraphs of at most about 80 words; parallel items become a list
findings.title: Split the handoff loop explanation into smaller units
findings.claim: One paragraph combines stop-reason handling, pending-response persistence, transfer selection and checkpointing, making the explanation difficult to follow on a phone.
findings.evidence: The paragraph contains 178 whitespace-separated words, more than twice STYLE.md's approximate 80-word limit.
findings.proposed_change: List the stop-reason cases, then use separate short paragraphs for saving pending calls and processing transfers. Preserve every behavior and identifier; rerun pytest after editing.

findings.checklist_item: Files: glossary terms point to the lesson that introduces them
findings.title: Combine the two glossary entries for superstep
findings.claim: The adjacent entries 'Super-step' and 'Superstep (LangGraph)' describe the same concept under different spellings, which can suggest they are separate terms.
findings.evidence: Both entries define one round of LangGraph execution. The existing entry links to 3.5; the new entry adds transactional and resume behavior from 8.3.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one entry with both spellings, preserve the checkpoint and recovery details, and link to 3.5 as the introduction and 8.3 for parallel failure handling. Run the link checker.
